page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, engineered for memory-intensive workloads requiring dedicated local storage and high network capacity. The system features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Memory capacity reaches 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In addition to high compute and memory capacity, the instance integrates 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-core and memory throughput. The server achieved a strong multi-core score in stress-ng tests alongside top-tier memory bandwidth metrics, reaching 215.93 GB/sec in uncached read operations and 95.7 GB/sec in uncached write operations. PassMark CPU and memory scores both placed in the top 25 percent. In application benchmarks, the platform generated 75.03 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and delivered 44.7 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core execution reflects moderate performance, with stress-ng single-core in the bottom 25 percent and Geekbench single-core in the middle 50 percent. Due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, LLM text generation rates remain low across models.

From an infrastructure perspective, the r5dn.24xlarge offers strong resource consolidation for demanding environments. Integrating 3600 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage eliminates external EBS storage latency and cost overheads for temporary processing tiers. The 100 Gbps network pipe ensures distributed applications do not bottleneck during node synchronizations. Because the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, deployments must account for data persistence architectures to protect against instance termination.

The hardware configuration suits large-scale distributed caching, real-time analytics engines, in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, and high-concurrency relational database workloads. It is also an effective target for data transformation pipelines and Clang build farms that require massive concurrent compilation capabilities alongside substantial memory headroom.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.1 GHz. Supported by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, 3600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance exhibits exceptional multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory bandwidth, and superior in-memory key-value processing throughput, achieving 75.03 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution and AI text generation tasks show lower relative performance due to processor architecture and the absence of accelerators, its dense memory and local storage array provide balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments. The server is well fitted for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching, high-throughput web serving, and intensive batch ETL processing.
